author: pgaudet
body:
Hi @Matrisome 

I managed to find all IDs, except for those of ECMX. Is there another name for this gene?

author: DaiqingChen
body:
Hi @pgaudet, sorry it took me a while to get back.
The reference for all genes are the same as ticket https://github.com/geneontology/go-ontology/issues/29269 , which is PMID: 25701227, I added to the request. As Alexandra and I reviewed the list again, we found some other genes and I added it to the list.

For ECMX, I realized that their CDS sequence was not found in human (PMID: 31947880). I found the ECMX gene in pig (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/100623862) and Amphibian (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/117368146).

author: pgaudet
body:
Hi @DaiqingChen 

For ECMX, I dont find anything in UniProt: https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb?query=ECMX
If you have identifiers that would allow me to make the annotations.

author: Matrisome
body:
@pgaudet I have done some digging and it is now believed that ECMX is a pseudogene (https://www.genenames.org/data/gene-symbol-report/#!/hgnc_id/55152) and so does not encode for a protein. We should thus exclude it from our annotations. 
@DaiqingChen , please make note of this and we should remove this entry from the matrisome list.

author: DaiqingChen
body:
> [@pgaudet](https://github.com/pgaudet) I have done some digging and it is now believed that ECMX is a pseudogene (https://www.genenames.org/data/gene-symbol-report/#!/hgnc_id/55152) and so does not encode for a protein. We should thus exclude it from our annotations. [@DaiqingChen](https://github.com/DaiqingChen) , please make note of this and we should remove this entry from the matrisome list.

Noted, ECMX is not in the matrisome list, only in the proteoglycan review.
